customManagers.description: habit-hooks pinned in mise.toml [env] (HABIT_HOOKS_VERSION); core and language plugin install in lockstep at this version. Matches the scaffolded repo's mise.toml and foundry's own mise/<stack>.toml templates.

Any mise.toml [env] pin annotated with a `# renovate: datasource=<ds> depName=<name>` comment on the line above (the Python template's mypy/pytest/pytest-cov/pip-audit/deptry). Reusable for any stack: annotate a pin and Renovate tracks it.

packageRules.description: Let a release settle for 7 days (the floor semgrep's renovate-missing-minimum-release-age rule enforces) before proposing it, to dodge just-published broken or compromised versions (supply-chain hygiene). Security fixes are exempted in the vulnerability rule below so they still land fast.
The CONTRACT says pin everything; Renovate is the update path. Keep Actions pinned to a digest and bump the digest + the trailing # vN comment together.
Actions majors need review, so they get their own grouped PR. Non-major Actions bumps fall through to the monthly all-non-major group.
Toolchain majors declared in mise.toml [tools] get their own grouped PR. Non-major toolchain bumps fall through to the monthly all-non-major group.
group:allNonMajor covers minor and patch only; fold digest and pin updates (mostly Actions digest bumps) into the same monthly PR so a month yields one non-major PR.

A major is a migration someone has to plan, and one PR per package across every repo was a daily flood of them. Majors wait on the Dependency Dashboard and become a PR only when ticked there; the security and Foundry rules below opt back out.

Security fixes land fast and on their own, labelled; exempt from minimumReleaseAge and from dashboard approval, even as a major, so a patched release is never held back. osvVulnerabilityAlerts adds OSV as a source, so a repo without GitHub alerts enabled still gets them. null (Renovate's own vulnerabilityAlerts default) rather than "0 seconds", which the semgrep rule rejects as not "N days", or false, which renovate-config-validator rejects.

Foundry is our own repo, so the 7-day hold (meant for strangers' compromised releases) only delays our own fixes. The reusable-workflow refs bump in one PR, any day and without dashboard approval even for a major; it merges itself once the consumer's gate passes. Still digest-pinned, so each bump is a gated change. null for the same semgrep/validator reasons as the vulnerability rule.

A Foundry major breaks the CONTRACT or the workflow interface, so it still lands as one PR but waits for a human instead of merging itself. minimumReleaseAge repeats the rule above only because semgrep's renovate-missing-minimum-release-age wants it on every package rule.

FOUNDRY_SCRIPTS_REF is not Renovate's to bump: setup:foundry-scripts verifies each script against the sha256 lines from that tag's template, which Renovate cannot compute, so its bump PR could only fail. Repos scaffolded before the template dropped its `# renovate:` annotation still carry it, hence switching the dependency off here rather than only in the templates. minimumReleaseAge only for the semgrep rule.
